searchText: <marcinbugaj> <@427491045308235776> , @jordibaylina , @amvlasov , @maximmenshikov , @tamirhemo , @jpwang let's circle back to the topic of zkVM IO interface. Here's the final proposal: https://github.com/eth-act/zkvm-standards/pull/8#issuecomment-3816759551 Left some comments -- in general I prefer this simpler approach to IO I guess `write_output` doesn't need to concatenate to a buffer, re <@381789485777682434> comment -- It could still do something like this internally: ```c HashState state; void write_output(const uint8_t* output, size_t size) { hash_update(&state, output, size); } void on_program_exit() { uint8_t final_hash[32]; hash_finalize(&state, final_hash); commit_public_input(final_hash); } ``` Yes, exactly ``` The program's output is the concatenation of buffers passed to successive calls to `write_output`. ``` means that the observable results is as if the buffers were concatenated. Do you want me to explicitly add words "observable"/"as if"? I think this might make it more explicit since I read it as a literal concatenation of buffers Fixed in: https://github.com/eth-act/zkvm-standards/pull/8/commits/b434dc70152c452140760cb6fed638e3af6bb060
